clue.text: Foreign novel left in university wings — not fair

indicators.note: the word in says the anagram and L go inside the wings of university
the wings of the word university are its two outside letters
something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters of novel are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disparaging verdict on a book in translation read at university: it is not fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as a book but is only letters to shuffle; 'fair' means good-looking, not just.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair here means attractive, so its negation describes something plain or ugly to look at.

clue.text: See 25
Supreme, timeless ancient city

indicators.note: time is abbreviated T, so timeless means that letter is dropped

parts.note: the supreme one is the best of all

explanation.surface: A supreme, ageless city of antiquity is being praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T (time) from THE BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a major city of ancient Egypt, and another of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Dire rep players "like concrete blocks"

indicators.note: dire means terrible, a signal that the letters of rep are badly rearranged

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast

explanation.surface: A review of awful repertory actors, damned as wooden as concrete blocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dire' turns REP into PRE; rep is short for a repertory theatre company.
explanation.definitionFit: Precast concrete is moulded into blocks or slabs before it reaches the building site.

clue.text: He hits you, you're smitten!

parts.note: the Greek god of love shoots arrows, and whoever he strikes falls in love, so being hit leaves you smitten

explanation.surface: Sounds like a brawl: get hit by him and you are struck down.
explanation.walkthrough: Smitten means both struck and infatuated; the archer of love does both at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek love god's arrows make their target fall for someone, the smitten sense of the clue.

clue.text: Concerned with teeth, after front teeth half removed by accident

indicators.note: the teeth word comes after the shortened front-teeth word
half the letters of the word are taken away, leaving the first four

parts.note: the incisors are the cutting teeth at the front of the mouth
dental means relating to teeth

explanation.surface: A dentist's note: front teeth half knocked out in an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: The front teeth are never printed: the solver must think of their name first, then keep its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incidental happens by chance, as a side effect, rather than by design.

clue.text: In that place, there's no earth hazard

indicators.note: no here means without, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: thereat is an old word meaning at that place
E is the abbreviation for earth on electrical plugs

explanation.surface: Somewhere with no solid ground underfoot is a danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' drops E (earth) from THEREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a danger or menace, something that might cause harm.

clue.text: Tinkered with the tune before record's initial release

indicators.note: tinkering with something means altering it, so these letters are rearranged
the initial of record's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A musician fiddled with the melody before the record came out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinkered with' turns THE TUNE into UNTETHE; 'initial' gives R from record's.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a tethered animal is to let it loose, freeing it from its rope.

clue.text: See 26 down
See 26
Recidivist supporter gains second cap

indicators.note: the supporter word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a backer supports a venture with money
a lid is a cap or cover

explanation.surface: A repeat offender's backer picks up a second hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A recidivist falls back into old bad habits or crime, which is relapsing.

clue.text: Saracen suspected accommodating count

indicators.note: the two words accommodate the answer, holding it within their letters

explanation.surface: A medieval Saracen is suspected of sheltering a nobleman, a count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' says the letters are tucked inside 'Saracen suspected'. 'count' looks like a nobleman, but it is a head count.
explanation.definitionFit: An official population survey is an exercise in counting people.

clue.text: Liable to be called "rank, heartless youth"

parts.note: rank and standing both mean status

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: a boy is a youth

explanation.surface: Someone is called a rank, heartless youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the O out of BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on standby is ready to be summoned at short notice, waiting for the call.

clue.text: Tourist destination resort on rocks

indicators.note: on the rocks means wrecked, signalling that the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday spot whose resort is on the rocks, failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' scrambles RESORT ON. Sorrento is a resort town on the Bay of Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian coastal town draws many holidaymakers to the Amalfi coast area.

clue.text: In colder surroundings, bum turns a certain colour

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes in the word for colder
the word for colder surrounds the other piece

parts.note: ... weather is cold, so rawer means colder

indicators.note: turns means the word bum is rotated, its first letter going round to the back

explanation.surface: Out in the cold, a backside turns a particular hue.
explanation.walkthrough: Raw weather is cold and damp, so the comparative serves for colder.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw umber is a brown earth pigment used by painters, a shade of dark brown.

clue.text: As a substitute for lane round top of field

parts.note: a byway is a minor lane
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the top of field is its first letter

explanation.surface: A detour by a country lane round the edge of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: BYWAY, O and the F at the top of field run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean serving as, in place of: a sofa by way of a bed.

clue.text: See 25
Weight thrown about, feeling irritated, tense

indicators.note: thrown about means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: itchy skin feels irritated

explanation.surface: Someone hurling weights around, irritated and tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown about' looks like an anagram signal; here it reverses WT to TW.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitchy person is nervous and jumpy, on edge.

clue.text: Stylish establishment that may need to be replaced

definitions.text: that may need to be replaced

parts.note: hip means fashionable
a joint is a bar or restaurant, slangily

explanation.surface: A trendy bar that is past it and due for a refit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is barely a definition: the body part is often replaced by surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn hips are commonly swapped for artificial ones in replacement surgery.

clue.text: Reached rocky area of France

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of reached are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Travellers arrived at a rugged part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' rearranges REACHED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardèche is a department of south-east France, known for its gorge.

clue.text: Hawk, parrot, cuckoo, incorporating origins of European dove?

indicators.note: the jumbled bird takes the two initials inside it
cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of parrot go mad
the origins of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A list of birds: hawk, parrot, cuckoo, with a European dove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' makes PRATOR from PARROT; 'incorporating' puts E and D inside. 'cuckoo' and 'parrot' look like birds in the list, but only 'Hawk' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk is a bird of prey, hunting other creatures for food.

clue.text: A sign there's work on the way

definitions.text: A sign there's work on the way

parts.words: A sign there's work on the way
parts.note: a road sign warns drivers that the surface is being dug up; 'on the way' sounds like soon to come

explanation.surface: An omen that a new job is coming soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way' reads as coming, but it is literal: the way is the road.
explanation.definitionFit: British road signs warn of works on the highway with this phrase.

clue.text: Car cut into bird

indicators.note: into puts the cutting word inside the bird

parts.note: a jay is a bird of the crow family
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A car has ploughed into a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalopy is an old, battered motor vehicle.

clue.text: Mix-up when modest Jack replaces Henry

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: humble means modest
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: Confusion arises when a modest Jack stands in for Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces' swaps H (henry) for J (jack) in HUMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumble is a disordered mess, a confusion of things.

clue.text: Complying with the standard electricity supply point in public transport?

parts.note: the mains is the household electricity supply

indicators.note: the point goes inside the transport word

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Asks if a tram's power socket meets the usual standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E (east) inside TRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream means conventional, following the prevailing norm rather than the fringe.

clue.text: Dismiss spring and end happily

parts.note: to turn out someone is to expel or dismiss them
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Sack someone in spring and it all ends on a happy note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season; it is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: When things finish with a good outcome, they are said to come right in the end.

clue.text: Lapdog or mongrel that scores several points

indicators.note: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A clever lapdog or mutt that wins points at a dog show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mongrel' rearranges LAPDOG OR. In rugby, a kick dropped and struck through the posts earns three points.
explanation.definitionFit: This rugby kick, struck on the half-volley over the bar, is worth three points.

clue.text: Establishment offering eg stock handling experience

definitions.text: Establishment offering eg stock handling experience

parts.words: Establishment offering eg stock handling experience
parts.note: a holiday place in the American West where city visitors try herding cattle; stock here is livestock, not shares

explanation.surface: Sounds like a firm offering training in handling stocks and shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' suggests finance, but it means farm animals.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of western holiday farm lets tourists play cowboy, rounding up cattle.

clue.text: See 15
Could be do's mid-point reached

parts.note: taking half of the word done, its first two letters, leaves this word

explanation.surface: A party's halfway mark has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: half of DONE is DO, which the clue prints.
explanation.definitionFit: A job that has reached its halfway point is partly finished, not yet complete.
